title: Judge leniency as IV for incarceration on recidivism

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy
- Method: Instrumental Variables (2SLS), using quasi-random assignment of defendants to judges with different incarceration propensities as the instrument.
- Setup:
  - Endogenous treatment: x (incarceration).
  - Outcome: y (recidivism within 3 years).
  - Instrument: z (judge “leniency/stringency” = leave-one-out judge incarceration rate; higher z implies a stricter judge).
  - Controls: baseline covariates (offense type, prior record, age), represented here by a summary index “controls”.
- Key assumptions:
  - Relevance: Judge stringency shifts the probability of incarceration (Cov(z, x | controls) ≠ 0). Expect a strong positive first stage.
  - Exclusion: Conditional on controls, judge assignment affects recidivism only through incarceration (no direct channels such as differential services or unobserved courtroom shocks).
  - Independence: As-if random assignment of cases to judges (z ⫫ potential outcomes and treatment, given controls).
  - Monotonicity: No defendants who would be incarcerated by a lenient judge but not by a strict judge (no “defiers”). The 2SLS estimates the LATE for compliers.
  - SUTVA: No interference across defendants and a well-defined treatment.

## 2. R Code
```r
# Packages
suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(readr)
  library(AER)        # ivreg
  library(sandwich)   # robust vcov
  library(lmtest)     # coeftest
})

# 1) Read data
path <- "experiments/exp_b/data/s23_data.csv"
df <- read_csv(path, col_types = cols())

# Inspect basic structure
n <- nrow(df)
cat("Sample size:", n, "\n")

# 2) OLS (naive, potentially biased)
ols <- lm(y ~ x + controls, data = df)
ols_rob <- coeftest(ols, vcov = vcovHC(ols, type = "HC1"))
ols_coef <- as.numeric(ols_rob["x", "Estimate"])
ols_se   <- as.numeric(ols_rob["x", "Std. Error"])
ols_p    <- as.numeric(ols_rob["x", "Pr(>|t|)"])
cat("\nNaive OLS: Effect of incarceration on recidivism (HC1 SE)\n")
cat(sprintf("  coef = %.4f, se = %.4f, p = %.4f\n", ols_coef, ols_se, ols_p))

# 3) First stage: x on z (+ controls)
fs <- lm(x ~ z + controls, data = df)
fs_rob <- coeftest(fs, vcov = vcovHC(fs, type = "HC1"))
# Extract z row robustly
if (!"z" %in% rownames(fs_rob)) stop("Instrument 'z' not found in first-stage results.")
fs_bz <- as.numeric(fs_rob["z", "Estimate"])
fs_se <- as.numeric(fs_rob["z", "Std. Error"])
fs_t  <- as.numeric(fs_rob["z", "t value"])
fs_F  <- fs_t^2
cat("\nFirst-stage (x ~ z + controls), HC1 SE\n")
cat(sprintf("  Effect of judge stringency on incarceration: %.4f (se = %.4f), t = %.2f, F = %.2f\n",
            fs_bz, fs_se, fs_t, fs_F))
if (is.finite(fs_F) && fs_F < 10) {
  cat("  Warning: First-stage F < 10 (potential weak instrument).\n")
}

# 4) 2SLS (main)
iv <- ivreg(y ~ x + controls | z + controls, data = df)
iv_rob <- coeftest(iv, vcov = vcovHC(iv, type = "HC1"))
if (!"x" %in% rownames(iv_rob)) stop("Endogenous regressor 'x' not found in IV results.")
iv_bx <- as.numeric(iv_rob["x", "Estimate"])
iv_se <- as.numeric(iv_rob["x", "Std. Error"])
iv_t  <- as.numeric(iv_rob["x", "t value"])
iv_p  <- as.numeric(iv_rob["x", "Pr(>|t|)"])
iv_ci <- iv_bx + c(-1, 1) * 1.96 * iv_se

cat("\nMain 2SLS (y ~ x + controls | z + controls), HC1 SE\n")
cat(sprintf("  LATE of incarceration on recidivism: %.4f (se = %.4f), t = %.2f, p = %.4f\n",
            iv_bx, iv_se, iv_t, iv_p))
cat(sprintf("  95%% CI: [%.4f, %.4f]\n", iv_ci[1], iv_ci[2]))

# 5) Reduced-form: y on z (+ controls)
rf <- lm(y ~ z + controls, data = df)
rf_rob <- coeftest(rf, vcov = vcovHC(rf, type = "HC1"))
if (!"z" %in% rownames(rf_rob)) stop("Instrument 'z' not found in reduced-form results.")
rf_bz <- as.numeric(rf_rob["z", "Estimate"])
rf_se <- as.numeric(rf_rob["z", "Std. Error"])
rf_p  <- as.numeric(rf_rob["z", "Pr(>|t|)"])
cat("\nReduced-form (y ~ z + controls), HC1 SE\n")
cat(sprintf("  Effect of judge stringency on recidivism: %.4f (se = %.4f), p = %.4f\n",
            rf_bz, rf_se, rf_p))

# 6) Basic robustness checks

# 6a) Add a quadratic term in controls to allow some nonlinearity
df$controls2 <- df$controls^2
iv_q <- ivreg(y ~ x + controls + controls2 | z + controls + controls2, data = df)
iv_q_rob <- coeftest(iv_q, vcov = vcovHC(iv_q, type = "HC1"))
iv_q_bx <- as.numeric(iv_q_rob["x", "Estimate"])
iv_q_se <- as.numeric(iv_q_rob["x", "Std. Error"])
cat("\nRobustness 1 (2SLS with quadratic control), HC1 SE\n")
cat(sprintf("  coef = %.4f, se = %.4f\n", iv_q_bx, iv_q_se))

# 6b) No-controls specification (relying purely on random assignment)
iv_nc <- ivreg(y ~ x | z, data = df)
iv_nc_rob <- coeftest(iv_nc, vcov = vcovHC(iv_nc, type = "HC1"))
iv_nc_bx <- as.numeric(iv_nc_rob["x", "Estimate"])
iv_nc_se <- as.numeric(iv_nc_rob["x", "Std. Error"])
cat("\nRobustness 2 (2SLS without controls), HC1 SE\n")
cat(sprintf("  coef = %.4f, se = %.4f\n", iv_nc_bx, iv_nc_se))

# 6c) Report standard first-stage diagnostics from AER (non-robust by default)
diag_sum <- summary(iv, diagnostics = TRUE)
cat("\nAER diagnostics (non-robust, for reference):\n")
print(diag_sum$diagnostics)
```

## 3. Expected Findings
- Sign: Positive. More incarceration (induced by stricter judges) is expected to increase recidivism among compliers, reflecting criminogenic effects of prison (disrupted labor market ties, exposure to criminal networks), once incapacitation effects fade.
- Magnitude: For a 0–1 recidivism outcome, many judge-IV studies find LATEs in the range of +0.05 to +0.15 (5–15 percentage points). With standardized or non-binary scaling (as suggested by the preview), expect a positive effect of similar order in standard-deviation units (roughly +0.10 to +0.30 SD). 
- First stage: Strong and positive; stricter judges substantially raise incarceration rates, with an F-stat typically > 10.

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: IV/2SLS — judge leniency instrument; LATE for marginal defendants; test exclusion restriction carefully
_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: Incarceration increases recidivism for marginal defendants (criminogenic effect)
_ground_truth.main_effect: Incarceration raises 3-year recidivism probability by ~15pp for compliers
